previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with alcoholic and hepatitis C-related cirrhosis was admitted for abdominal pain and possible gastrointestinal bleeding after reporting melena. Initial evaluation revealed stable hemoglobin and no active bleeding on EGD, which showed esophageal varices and portal gastropathy. She presented with mild hepatic encephalopathy, likely triggered by recent initiation of gabapentin and hydroxyzine, both of which were discontinued, leading to improved mental status. Abdominal pain was managed with tramadol and attributed to alcoholic gastritis or portal gastropathy. A known 2.6 cm hepatocellular carcinoma was confirmed, and outpatient TACE therapy was scheduled. Pancytopenia remained stable and was attributed to underlying cirrhosis and alcohol use. The patient was discharged home in improved condition with instructions to avoid alcohol, continue lactulose and rifaximin, and follow up with liver clinic and psychiatry.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with left lobe liver HCC that needs selective
tace. Patient has decompensated cirrhosis  // Please do selective TACE

COMPARISON:  MRCP ___, CT abdomen and pelvis ___.

TECHNIQUE:   OPERATORS: Dr. ___ radiology fellow) and
Dr. ___ radiology attending) performed the procedure.  The
attending, Dr. ___ supervised the trainee during the key
components of the procedure and has reviewed and agrees with the trainee's
findings

ANESTHESIA: Moderate sedation was provided by administrating divided doses of
75mcg of fentanyl and 2 mg of midazolam throughout the total intra-service
time of 90 min during which the patient's hemodynamic parameters were
continuously monitored by an independent trained radiology nurse. 1% lidocaine
was injected in the skin and subcutaneous tissues overlying the access site.

MEDICATIONS: Fentanyl, midazolam, 30 mg of Toradol.

CONTRAST: 110 ml of Optiray contrast.

FLUOROSCOPY TIME AND DOSE:  27.8 min, 421 mGy

PROCEDURE:
1. Right common femoral artery access.
2. Common hepatic arteriogram with cone beam CT.
3. Selective second order LHA branch (Segment II) arteriogram.
4. Selective second order LHA branch (Segment II) chemoembolization (DEB-TACE
with Oncozene).
5. Right common femoral arteriogram with and Angio-Seal closure.

PROCEDURE DETAILS: Following the discussion of the risks, benefits and
alternatives to the procedure, written informed consent was obtained from the
patient. The patient was then brought to the angiography suite and placed
supine on the exam table.  A pre-procedure time-out was performed per ___
protocol. The right was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.

Using palpatory and fluoroscopic guidance, the right common femoral artery was
punctured using a micropuncture set at the level of the mid-femoral head. A
0.018 wire was passed easily into the vessel lumen. A small skin incision was
made over the needle. Then the inner dilator and wire were removed and a
___ wire was advanced under fluoroscopy into the aorta. The micropuncture
sheath was exchanged for a 5 ___ sheath which was attached to a continuous
heparinized saline side arm flush.

A C2 glide Cobra catheter was advanced over ___ wire into the aorta. The
wire was removed and the celiac artery was selectively cannulated and a small
contrast injection was made to confirm position.  The C2 was advanced into the
common hepatic artery using a glidewire. A common hepaticarteriogram and
cone-beam CT was performed.  Exact contributions to the target tumor were
difficult to assess, therefore a more selective LHA branch angiogram was
required for diagnostic evaluation. An STC microcatheter pre-loaded with a
Headliner wire was used to access a second order branch of the left hepatic
artery and a segment 2 hepatic arteriogram was performed. Segment 2 hepatic
arterial embolization was performed.

CONE-BEAM CT:  A rotational cone beam CT was performed to evaluate the
relationship between the tumor and hepatic arterial supply. Multiplanar CT
images were reconstructed and 3D volume-rendered images of the arterial
anatomy required post-processing on an independent workstation under direct
physician ___ (Dr. ___. These images were used in the
interpretation and reporting of this procedure.

All materials used in chemotherapy delivery were disposed of per departmental
protocol. The catheters were then removed.  Right common femoral arteriogram
was performed from the sheath. A 6 ___ Angio-Seal closure device was used.
Hemostasis was achieved. Sterile dressings were applied. The patient tolerated
the procedure well.

FINDINGS: 

1. Conventional hepatic arterial anatomy.
2.  Pre-embolization cone beam CT arteriogram combined with selective LHA
branch angiogram showing tumoral supply from segment II artery. Mild bibasilar
atelectasis. Aortic calcifications.
3.  DEB-TACE to Segment II tumor via selective catheterization.
4.  Patent right common femoral artery with anatomy suitable for Angio-Seal
closure device deployment.

IMPRESSION: 

Selective trans-arterial chemoembolization of Segment II tumor.

RECOMMENDATION:  1 month followup multiphasic MRI of the liver to evaluate for
tumor response.
